questions.question: 1. You must adept yourself to new situations. 2. He is adept in the art of dancing. 1. You must adept yourself to new situations. 2. He is adept in the art of dancing.
questions.questionHtml:
1. You must adept yourself to new situations.

1. You must adept yourself to new situations.

2. He is adept in the art of dancing.
questions.solution:
Sentence 1: ❌ You must adept yourself to new situations.
✔ You must adapt yourself to new situations.

Why?

  • Adept = adjective (skilled, proficient)

  • Adapt = verb (to adjust/change)

You need a verb here, so adapt is correct, not adept.

Sentence 2: ✔ He is adept in the art of dancing. ✅

Why?

  • Adept is correctly used as an adjective meaning highly skilled.

  • It is followed by in (sometimes at is also acceptable).

✔ Examples:

  • She is adept in mathematics.

  • He is adept at handling crises.
